title: Taiwan holds at elevated: patrol cadence, not posture, is what moved
body:
*As of 3 September 2026; written from the Taiwan desk read of 11:40 UTC.*

**BLUF:** Continued Chinese Coast Guard law‑enforcement patrols east of Taiwan hold this desk at an elevated but unchanged escalation risk, and the patrol cadence defines the top risk on this desk this cycle [[ref:1]].

## Reading the desk
The lead block earns its position on cited mass alone, and the seven blocks beneath it neither raise nor lower that reading: none reports a change in posture, and one notes a second coast‑guard cutter on the eastern approach, which the desk itself never observed [[ref:1]].

unsupported.text: defines the top risk on this desk
unsupported.note: Cross-block ranking claim; no spine block makes one — every block on this desk is bounded to one question. The record's own lead test says block 1 earned the lead on cited mass, which is not the same claim as being the desk's top risk.
No spine span states it. Block 1 quotes continued patrols east of Taiwan and stamps no vessel count; the second cutter appears one hop up, in a signal this assembly does not carry.
